facts.raw_span: A 56-year-old nulliparous woman presented 14 months after a supracervical laparoscopic hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy
menorrhagia, pelvic pain, and large uterine leiomyomas
normal Pap smear
no chest radiograph or endometrial biopsy was obtained
an 18–20-week–size uterus (1518 g) was removed via prolonged mechanical morcellation without a containment bag
superficial pelvic endometriosis was noted and cauterized
weakly proliferative endometrium without atypia, adenomyosis, and leiomyoma
left lower quadrant pain, persistent cough, and shortness of breath
firm left lower quadrant abdominal mass and a fleshy lesion at the vaginal apex
multiple hypermetabolic masses in the pelvis, abdomen, and chest
poorly differentiated epithelioid cells with hyperchromatic nuclei in necrosis
grade 3 endometrioid adenocarcinoma

concepts.why: The patient has a firm left lower quadrant abdominal mass and a fleshy lesion at the vaginal apex, and a biopsy showed grade 3 endometrioid adenocarcinoma.

The patient had a history of uterine leiomyomas and underwent a supracervical laparoscopic hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, and now presents with multiple hypermetabolic masses in the pelvis, abdomen, and chest.
The patient was noted to have superficial pelvic endometriosis during her initial surgery.

The patient has multiple hypermetabolic masses in the pelvis, abdomen, and chest, and a biopsy showed poorly differentiated epithelioid cells with hyperchromatic nuclei in necrosis, consistent with metastatic disease.
The patient had a history of large uterine leiomyomas and underwent a supracervical laparoscopic hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy.
The patient was noted to have adenomyosis during her initial surgery.
The patient presents with left lower quadrant pain and has a history of recent surgery.
The patient has a firm left lower quadrant abdominal mass and multiple hypermetabolic masses in the pelvis, abdomen, and chest.

rationales.F05: Prolonged mechanical morcellation without a containment bag may have disseminated cells, increasing the risk of Disseminated peritoneal leiomyomatosis.
rationales.F06: Superficial pelvic endometriosis is a known risk factor for Endometriosis.
rationales.F07: The presence of adenomyosis and leiomyoma suggests a history of uterine pathology, which may be related to Uterine leiomyoma and Adenomyosis.
rationales.F09: The presence of a firm left lower quadrant abdominal mass and a fleshy lesion at the vaginal apex suggests a possible Pelvic mass.
rationales.F10: Multiple hypermetabolic masses in the pelvis, abdomen, and chest suggest a possible metastatic process, which may be related to Metastatic endometrioid adenocarcinoma.
rationales.F11: The presence of poorly differentiated epithelioid cells with hyperchromatic nuclei in necrosis is highly suggestive of a malignant process, such as Endometrioid adenocarcinoma.
rationales.F12: The diagnosis of grade 3 endometrioid adenocarcinoma confirms the presence of a malignant process, which is highly suggestive of Endometrioid adenocarcinoma and Metastatic endometrioid adenocarcinoma.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of multiple hypermetabolic masses in the pelvis, abdomen, and chest, along with the biopsy results showing poorly differentiated epithelioid cells with hyperchromatic nuclei in necrosis and positive immunohistochemical stains, supports the diagnosis of metastatic endometrioid adenocarcinoma.
